Ancient Wall Found Under Paris Hotel Dates to Gallo-Roman Period

A wall dating from the Gallo-Roman period has been discovered beneath a hotel on the Ile de la Cite in Paris, near Notre Dame Cathedral. The stone-and-wood wall, approximately 20 meters long, was unearthed in the city center. The Ministry of Culture stated it may be a fragment of the rampart of Lutetia, built by the Gallic Parisii tribe, potentially confirming the city's original settlement.
